Opening

GROW · SCIENCE · Autumn 2 · Week 6 · LESSON A · 2 MINUTES

Rover Rescue: Plan a Fair Test

Learning objective

I can plan a fair surface test, use repeated distance results and explain what the evidence supports.

Success looks like

  • Change the surface and keep the release conditions consistent.
  • Measure travel in centimetres from the same origin and rover point.
  • Compare all repeats and state a sensible limitation.

A rescue rover needs a reliable route. Your task is not to make the longest run; it is to make the comparison fair.

Two separate lessons

A · Explore and explain · 40 minutes

B · Rover Evidence Lab · 40 minutes

Stop after Lesson A. Lesson B has its own start and exit.

Point, speak, sign, move cards, draw, write or direct an adult. Choose one route; equivalent science evidence does not require a written conversion.

I do

GROW · SCIENCE · Autumn 2 · Week 6 · LESSON A · 7 MINUTES

Watch, predict, explain

Predict, model, explain

We changed ___. We measured ___ in cm. We kept ___ the same. The results support ___ in this setup.

Make a prediction. Change one view, then use a label to explain what you notice.

Change the run-out surface. Keep the rover and release height the same.

Worked explanation · reveal after thinking

The rover is a classroom contact-resistance model, not a reproduction of Mars gravity or soil. Rolling resistance and other contacts matter; do not assert a universal roughness rule. Supplied 48/51/49 cm and 27/29/28 cm values are invented teaching data, not class measurements. Prediction and result are different.

Local explainer · 32 seconds · silent with captions

Use instead of part of the demonstration. It never autoplays and needs no internet.

Full text / no-video alternative

00–08 seconds · Define the test
Change the run-out surface. Keep the rover and release height the same.

08–16 seconds · Fix the measurement
Measure from the marked ramp exit to the same point on the stopped rover, in centimetres.

16–24 seconds · Repeat fairly
Complete three no-push trials on each surface. Keep all six raw results.

24–32 seconds · Review a conclusion
Compare the repeated results, explain variation and keep the conclusion within this setup.

Read the card clues

Surface: Compare the chosen smooth and fabric run-out surfaces.

Travel distance: Measure centimetres from the marked origin to the rover’s front.

Rover: Use the same unpowered rover in each trial.

Release mark: Release without a push from the same mark.

Ramp height: Keep the ramp at the same secured height.

You do

GROW · SCIENCE · Autumn 2 · Week 6 · LESSON A · 10 MINUTES

Use the evidence yourself

Supported · use one response mode

1. Plan the variables

Place the change, measure and keep cards under headings.

Help: Surface / distance / same setup.

2. Make a usable method

Order release → stop → measure → record.

Help: No push from the marked start.

3. Prepare the record

Point to six blank trial spaces and one safety step.

Help: Two surfaces × three trials.

Standard · use one response mode

1. Plan the variables

Write a test question, prediction and three controls.

Help: How does surface affect travel distance?

2. Make a usable method

Write a method another adult can follow, with three trials per surface.

Help: Measure in cm from the ramp exit.

3. Prepare the record

Draw a six-result table and name a practical risk control.

Help: Clear lane; secured low ramp.

Stretch · use one response mode

1. Plan the variables

Justify each control and distinguish a prediction from a conclusion.

Help: Do not reveal supplied results as a prediction.

2. Make a usable method

Specify ruler origin, rover reference point and handling of unusual trials.

Help: Record a possible method problem before repeating.

3. Prepare the record

Explain how the plan separates surface effects from changing release conditions.

Help: Same release height and vehicle.

Workshop

GROW · SCIENCE · Autumn 2 · Week 6 · LESSON B · 20 MINUTES

Gather and use evidence

Use a low secured ramp on the floor or inside a bounded tray, one unpowered toy rover and a clear stop lane. Keep hands out of the run; collect only once stopped. No high drops or projectiles. An adult can release and measure, or use the complete supplied-data route.

4 min · Recheck the release and measurement method.
20 min · Carry out or direct six safe trials, or analyse the supplied teaching dataset. Label your evidence source.
2 min · Check controls, units and all raw values.
6 min · Compare repeated distances, qualify the conclusion and improve one method detail.
StepConsistent procedure
1 · Set upOne secured ramp, rover and marked measurement origin
2 · TrialRelease from the mark without pushing; allow it to stop
3 · MeasureMeasure to the same rover point in cm; record the raw result
4 · RepeatThree trials per surface; record any method issue

Supported route

Direct an adult, read one distance or point to the longer set. Use all supplied values with help; explain one control.

Standard route

Record three trials per surface or use the supplied set. Compare the intervals, give a conclusion and identify a limitation.

Stretch route

Calculate means (about 49.3 and 28 cm) and numerical ranges (3 and 2 cm). Discuss variation and how extra repeats differ from testing extra surfaces.

Supplied resources · read or print

Run the test · practical checklist

Before release

Secure a low ramp and clear a bounded stopping lane. Agree an adult stop signal. Use the same rover, release point and surface starting position.

For each trial

Release without pushing. Wait for the rover to stop. Measure from the ramp-exit mark to the same point on the rover. Record the distance in cm before resetting.

Repeats and problems

Three trials on each surface. Retain every raw result. Record a collision, push or shifted ruler; discuss whether a justified extra trial is needed.

Supplied-data option

Use the supplied table instead of running equipment. Label it invented teaching data, not your own measurements.

Conclusion frame

In this setup, ________ travelled farther because the evidence shows ________. A limitation is ________.

Check

GROW · SCIENCE · Autumn 2 · Week 6 · LESSON B · 2 MINUTES

Check one piece of evidence

Check one piece of evidence

Are there six raw values with cm? Was each measured from the same origin to the same rover point? Is the source labelled measured or supplied?

Worked explanation · reveal after thinking

Supplied data: smooth 48, 51, 49 cm, mean ≈49.3 cm, range 3 cm; fabric 27, 29, 28 cm, mean 28 cm, range 2 cm. All smooth trials go farther here. Contact resistance is a plausible reason under the controlled setup. Do not claim the model establishes performance on Mars.

Improve one science explanation

Improve the science, not the amount of writing

Retain raw results. Add a missing control or unit, investigate an unusual run, or replace “always” with a conclusion about this setup.

Exit

Two checks to finish

Supported · 2 questions

1. Use the evidence

Supplied smooth results are 48, 51, 49 cm; fabric 27, 29, 28 cm. Which went farther here?

Help beside the question
Point, choose or say. Compare every result.

Answer guidance

Answer: Smooth; all smooth distances exceed all fabric distances.

2. Limit

Choose: this rover and these surfaces, or every rover on Mars?

Help beside the question
Only this comparison was made.

Answer guidance

Answer: This rover and these surfaces.

Standard · 2 questions

1. Use the evidence

Supplied smooth results are 48, 51, 49 cm; fabric 27, 29, 28 cm. Which went farther here?

Help beside the question
Compare every result.

Answer guidance

Answer: Smooth; all smooth distances exceed all fabric distances.

2. Limit

State one limitation of the conclusion.

Help beside the question
Think one rover, two surfaces and three repeats.

Answer guidance

Answer: It applies to this setup; it does not establish all rovers/surfaces or conditions on Mars.

Stretch · 2 questions

1. Use the evidence

Compare the means of the two supplied datasets.

Help beside the question
Add each group and divide by three.

Answer guidance

Answer: Smooth 148/3 ≈ 49.3 cm; fabric 84/3 = 28 cm; difference ≈ 21.3 cm.

2. Limit

State one limitation of the conclusion.

Help beside the question
Use an accurate science word. Think one rover, two surfaces and three repeats.

Answer guidance

Answer: It applies to this setup; it does not establish all rovers/surfaces or conditions on Mars.

Knowledge organiser

GROW Science · Autumn 2 · Week 6 · Shared resource · Shared resource

Learning objective

I can plan a fair surface test, use repeated distance results and explain what the evidence supports.

Key words

variable — something that can change

control — a condition kept the same

repeat — another trial using the same method

range — largest value minus smallest value

conclusion — an answer supported by the results

Remember

  • Change only the tested surface in this comparison.
  • Use the same rover, ramp, release mark and no-push release.
  • Measure from one origin to the same part of the rover.
  • Keep raw results; investigate unusual readings rather than selecting only convenient ones.

Success looks like

  • Change the surface and keep the release conditions consistent.
  • Measure travel in centimetres from the same origin and rover point.
  • Compare all repeats and state a sensible limitation.

We changed ___. We measured ___ in cm. We kept ___ the same. The results support ___ in this setup.

Ramp height

Answers · A · Standard

GROW Science · Autumn 2 · Week 6 · Lesson A · Standard

Four-question arrival

1. Change one thing: Surface only.

2. Measure: Centimetres.

3. Release: Release from one mark without pushing.

4. Repeat: Repeats show whether results vary and whether a pattern is consistent.

Two-check exit

1. Fair plan: Change surface; measure distance in cm; keep rover, ramp or release constant.

2. Repeat and measure: Use the same origin and rover reference point for three trials per surface.

Staff · feedback and access

GROW Science · Autumn 2 · Week 6 · Shared resource · Shared resource

Audience and response

The lesson teacher is the named adult audience. Hear or read the pupil’s own science response. A click, downloaded file or completed box is not evidence that a request was heard.

Respond within the existing task

Offer reading help, fewer cards at once, clearer labels, an adult-directed model or additional thinking time. Say what can and cannot change, then check whether the adjustment helped.

No additional pupil artefact

A response can be spoken, pointed, signed, drawn or written. Do not require a separate Lundy record, signature or written conversion of an oral response.

An optional pupil-owned note such as “What I said, and what it changed” may be used in existing work. It is not a requirement. If scribing, keep the pupil’s own words; the adult is an audience, not a verifier.

Keep assessment honest

Use current school recording practice and unit criteria separately. This pack does not certify an award. Do not infer a policy code from automated checking or a download.
